catalog_quote: Stress is contrastive, both in placement and in quality. Each word has at least one stressed syllable, but may have more. 2.4.1 Contrastive placement of stress The following pairs illustrate contrast in placement of stress: íimaca ‘he said’, iimáca ‘he slept’; iicáca ‘he sees’, íicaca ‘he digs’; úcunái ‘herons’, ucúaca ‘she toasted (cassava)’; yéeba ‘its placenta’, yeebá ‘he responds’. One important restriction on stress placement is that stress does not occur on the second of two identical vowels in sequence. 2.4.2 Contrastive quality of stress There is a contrast between high stress, marked by high tone V́, and low stress, marked by low tone V̀. The following pairs show this contrast: nuyáaca ‘I ate’, nuyàaca ‘I wove’; úuluí ‘cashew fruit’, ùuluì ‘her knee’ ...
